candidates.evidence: Strong band at 353.0 cm-1 (E2g/E' with 2LA(M) overlapped, FWHM ~8.5) and weaker A1g/A1' at 415.3 cm-1 (FWHM ~7.4) at 532 nm. These match the WS2 fingerprint. Si at 520.9 cm-1 shows the SiO2/Si substrate.
The E2g/A1g pair would sit near 250 cm-1. The data has no band there.
The pair would sit at 383/408 cm-1. The observed bands are at 353/415 cm-1, which does not match.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given. This is an identify task.

peaks.assignment: E2g(Γ) / E'(Γ) in-plane mode, overlapped with 2LA(M)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit of spectrum.csv. Assignment follows Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), which reports E2g at ~356 and 2LA(M) at ~352 cm-1 for WS2 at 532 nm. The two cannot be separated in this single-polarization spectrum.
Lorentzian fit. Assignment follows Berkdemir et al. 2013 and Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013), which report A1g at ~418-420 cm-1.
Berkdemir et al. 2013. A fit in the 150-320 cm-1 region found no significant peak above the noise, so this is not reported as measured.

properties.name: A1g - E2g separation
properties.source: 415.3 - 353.0 from the fit. Monolayer WS2 is ~61-62 and bulk ~64-65 (Berkdemir 2013), so this value points to thin material (monolayer to few-layer).

properties.name: A1g/E2g(+2LA) intensity ratio
properties.source: Peak heights from the fit. The low A1g relative intensity and the strong 2LA/E2g band are typical of monolayer or few-layer WS2 at 532 nm. The 2LA(M) overlap inflates the 353 cm-1 band, so the ratio is not clean.

properties.name: Layer number
properties.value: Probably mono- to few-layer; not determined uniquely
properties.source: Based on the mode separation and intensity ratio above.

artifacts.type: Si substrate line (520.9 cm-1), not a sample mode

citations: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013): Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman spectroscopy
Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013): Lattice dynamics and Raman of WS2 layers
limits: Only one polarization and no angle-resolved data, so the polarization pattern of each mode is not determined.
E2g and 2LA(M) overlap at ~353 cm-1 and could not be separated. The E2g position is uncertain by a few cm-1.
Layer number is only constrained. The spectrum cannot tell monolayer from bilayer or trilayer without PL or low-frequency shear/breathing modes. The 60-150 cm-1 region shows no resolved modes.
The spectrum is noisy (about 10% of the Si peak height), so weak features such as LA(M) and combination bands could not be resolved.
Strain or doping could shift the peaks by 1-3 cm-1, and the data cannot separate these effects from thickness.
No cosmic-ray spikes were found. The only outlier points belong to the Si line.
